units.title: Information Systems in the Enterprise
topics: The organisation pyramid and decision levels
Seeing information systems: machines, pyramids and flows

sections.title: The organisation pyramid and decision levels
Seeing information systems: machines, pyramids and flows

summary: Data become information when processed in context, and knowledge when combined with experience; good information is accurate, timely, relevant, complete, consistent, secure and worth its cost.
A system has inputs, processes, outputs, feedback and control inside a boundary; an IS has hardware, software, data, procedures and people.
Decisions are structured, semi-structured or unstructured and are made at operational, tactical and strategic levels.
TPS record events (batch or online, ACID); MIS summarise them; DSS model what-ifs; ESS display KPIs; KMS share knowledge.
Islands of information are fixed by integration and enterprise systems.

units.title: Strategy and Competitive Advantage
topics: Strategy and the role of information systems
Aligning IS strategy with business strategy
Seeing strategy: forces, concentration, chains and networks

sections.title: Strategy and the role of information systems
Aligning IS strategy with business strategy
Seeing strategy: forces, concentration, chains and networks

summary: Strategic information systems change the firm's competitive position; sustainability requires data, relationships, scale or processes that rivals cannot easily copy.
Porter's five forces (entrants, suppliers, buyers, substitutes, rivalry) can be scored; HHI measures concentration, and a merger raises it by twice the product of the shares.
The value chain locates IS value in primary and support activities and in the interfaces with suppliers and customers.
Generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and focus; switching costs, lock-in and network effects reinforce them.
Alignment, CSFs and BPR connect IS investment to business goals.

units.title: Enterprise Applications - ERP, CRM and Supply Chain Management
topics: Seeing enterprise systems: one database, costs and the bullwhip

sections.title: Seeing enterprise systems: one database, costs and the bullwhip

summary: ERP shares one database across finance, sales, procurement, inventory, manufacturing and HR; implementation may be big bang, phased, parallel or pilot, and weighted scoring supports vendor choice.
CRM has operational, analytical and collaborative forms; RFM segments customers.
SCM coordinates material, information and money flows. EOQ = √(2DS/H); safety stock = z·σ_d·√L; reorder point = demand × L + safety stock.
The bullwhip effect amplifies variance up the chain by 1 + 2L/p + 2L²/p² per stage; sharing demand data and shortening lead times reduce it.

units.title: Decision Support, Business Intelligence and Knowledge Management
topics: Decisions under risk: payoff tables and EMV
Decision trees and the value of a pilot
Seeing decisions: steps, payoffs, trees and warehouses

sections.title: Decisions under risk: payoff tables and EMV
Decision trees and the value of a pilot
Seeing decisions: steps, payoffs, trees and warehouses

summary: Decisions follow intelligence, design, choice and implementation; DSS support each phase.
Decision tables expose missing or contradictory rules; 2ⁿ combinations must each match exactly one rule.
Under risk use EMV; EVPI bounds the value of information. Under uncertainty use maximin, maximax, Laplace, Hurwicz or minimax regret, chosen to fit the risk attitude.
Decision trees are solved by rolling back; information is valuable only if it can change the decision.
BI relies on ETL, warehouses, star schemas, OLAP and KPIs; KM converts tacit and explicit knowledge (SECI).

units.title: e-Business, e-Commerce and Digital Payments in Nepal
topics: The online customer funnel and unit economics
Seeing e-business: funnels, unit economics and netting

sections.title: The online customer funnel and unit economics
Seeing e-business: funnels, unit economics and netting

summary: e-Business covers all online business processes; e-commerce is online trade; models include B2C, B2B, C2C, G2C and m-commerce with revenue by margin, commission, subscription or advertising.
Funnel metrics, CAC and LTV tell whether growth is profitable; sanity-check the assumptions.
A payment passes through authorisation, clearing and settlement; NRB licenses PSOs and PSPs under the Payment and Settlement Act 2075.
NCHL (NPI, ConnectIPS), Fonepay (switch and QR), wallets and banks form the retail payment network; multilateral netting reduces settlement transfers.
Always verify payment status server-side with the gateway before fulfilment.

units.title: Security and Control of Information Systems
topics: Seeing security: factors, risk arithmetic, entropy and recovery

sections.title: Seeing security: factors, risk arithmetic, entropy and recovery

summary: Security aims at confidentiality, integrity and availability; controls are preventive, detective or corrective.
ALE = AV × EF × ARO; a safeguard is justified when the ALE it removes exceeds its cost.
Entropy L × log₂ N measures password strength; use MFA and salted slow hashes.
E-commerce security relies on TLS, a gateway, server-side verification, fraud rules and secure code.
RPO and RTO drive backup and recovery design; audit and the Electronic Transactions Act supply oversight and legal frame.

units.title: Developing and Justifying Information Systems
topics: Seeing investment decisions: cash flows, NPV, TCO and break-even

sections.title: Seeing investment decisions: cash flows, NPV, TCO and break-even

summary: Choose build, buy, customise or outsource on fit, cost, skills and risk; failures are usually organisational.
Discount cash flows; accept projects with NPV > 0 or IRR above the required rate; payback and ROI are simple supplements.
TCO includes all lifetime costs; compare options at present value.
Break-even volume = fixed cost ÷ contribution margin.
Change management and post-implementation review complete the investment cycle.
